samples.summary: logout()'s new local-data erase is reached from fetchWithAuth's 401 arm, so an involuntary session expiry destroys locally persisted unsent work
samples.evidence: The diff adds `await eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` inside `logout()` (packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:105). The user-initiated logout (packages/frontend/src/components/nav-user.tsx:41) is not the only caller: `fetchWithAuth` calls `logout({ redirect: false, showSuccessToast: false, suppressFailure: true })` at packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:229 whenever any authenticated request returns 401 and the refresh fails. That path is an *involuntary* sign-out (access token expiry, backend restart, session invalidated), and it now runs `dropAllForUser`, deleting every locally stored snapshot/log AND every archive for the user — including edits that never reached the server, which is precisely the work this feature exists to preserve. Nothing at that call site distinguishes "user asked to sign out" from "token expired"; the erase should be gated on the deliberate logout, or at least spare archives.

samples.summary: The Settings "Save documents on this device" switch ships live while supportsClientKey() is permanently false on the pinned dependency, so the toggle promises persistence that never happens
samples.evidence: `supportsClientKey()` requires `@yorkie-js/react` >= 0.7.23 (packages/frontend/src/lib/yorkie-capabilities.ts, MinClientKeyVersion), and the pin is `"@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22"` (packages/frontend/package.json:65). `useDurableDocument` puts `supportsClientKey()` first in `eligible` (packages/frontend/src/lib/use-durable-document.ts), so no document is ever durable on this build. The new Settings section is not gated on the same capability: it renders unconditionally and its copy claims "Keeps edits that have not reached the server on this device, so they survive a reload or a crash while you are offline." A user who enables it gets no persistence at all, and the chip never reaches `saved-locally`. docs/tasks/active/20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:242-246 records the gate being closed as deliberate, but the user-visible switch is the one consumer not behind it.

samples.summary: A mid-session durability flip swaps CollabDocumentProvider between a nested and the ambient YorkieProvider, remounting the DocumentProvider and the entire editor subtree under it
samples.evidence: `CollabDocumentProvider` returns `inner` directly when not durable and `<DurableYorkieProvider>{inner}</DurableYorkieProvider>` when durable. React sees a different element type at that position, so flipping `durable` unmounts and remounts the whole `DocumentProvider` subtree. `useDurableDocument` re-evaluates on every preference change (`useOfflinePersistenceEnabled`) and on `standDown()`, and packages/frontend/src/lib/use-durable-document.test.tsx explicitly asserts "becomes durable without a reload". The consumers below are full editors that assume a stable provider for the document's lifetime — e.g. packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:578 and packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:176 both comment that the Yorkie document "belongs to the enclosing DocumentProvider and outlives" their effects. Toggling the Settings switch (in this tab or another, since the preference is cross-tab) while an editor is open therefore tears down the attached client and the editor state, and any change still queued in the old client goes with it.

samples.summary: dropAllForUser purges entries for documents that are open right now, unlike every other delete path in the same store, and it is invoked from the preference watcher while editors are attached
samples.evidence: `collectStale` (packages/frontend/src/lib/wafflebase-doc-store.ts:876) and `evictOldest` (:1045) both skip entries for which `isLive(docKey)` is true, with a doc-comment explaining that deleting under a live SDK client makes every later append vanish silently. `dropAllForUser` (:842) applies no such check: it calls `purge()` for every header key of the user. It is now called from `watchForOfflineDisable` (packages/frontend/src/lib/offline-erase.ts) the moment the Settings switch goes off — a cross-tab event, so a tab with a durable document attached can have its live entry deleted underneath it, and from `appendChange`'s point of view the missing header is the contract's silent "no base" success (the key is never added to `evicted`, so no rejection is raised to make the SDK re-base).

samples.summary: OfflineRuntime runs unconditionally for every signed-in user, opening/creating the IndexedDB database and sweeping on every session even though nothing can ever be durable on this build
samples.evidence: `PrivateRoute` mounts `<OfflineRuntime userId={String(me.id)} />` (packages/frontend/src/PrivateRoute.tsx:35) with no check of the preference or of `supportsClientKey()`. The effect constructs a `WafflebaseDocStore` and calls `collectStale()` and `listRecoverableWork()`, both of which `indexedDB.open(...)` the `wafflebase-offline` database — creating it for every user of the app, including the overwhelming majority who never enable the setting and, on the current pin, everyone. Cheap but not free: a database handle and two transactions per login, plus a `rememberOfflineUser` side effect that arms the logout erase.

samples.summary: OfflineRuntime's cleanup clears the recorded identity, so a sign-out that unmounts PrivateRoute before logout()'s erase runs silently skips the erase it promises
samples.evidence: `rememberOfflineUser(undefined)` runs in OfflineRuntime's effect cleanup, and `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` returns immediately when no identity is recorded (packages/frontend/src/lib/offline-erase.ts, `if (!who) return`). Any path where the `["me"]` query in packages/frontend/src/PrivateRoute.tsx:13 resolves to no user (or the route unmounts) before `logout()` reaches its erase leaves `signedInUserId` undefined, so the "signing out deletes local content on a shared device" guarantee quietly becomes a no-op. I could not confirm the exact interleaving for the `fetchWithAuth` 401 path, where both the query invalidation and the `logout()` call are in flight.

finding.summary: logout()'s new local-data erase is reached from fetchWithAuth's 401 arm, so an involuntary session expiry destroys locally persisted unsent work
finding.evidence: The diff adds `await eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` inside `logout()` (packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:105). The user-initiated logout (packages/frontend/src/components/nav-user.tsx:41) is not the only caller: `fetchWithAuth` calls `logout({ redirect: false, showSuccessToast: false, suppressFailure: true })` at packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:229 whenever any authenticated request returns 401 and the refresh fails. That path is an *involuntary* sign-out (access token expiry, backend restart, session invalidated), and it now runs `dropAllForUser`, deleting every locally stored snapshot/log AND every archive for the user — including edits that never reached the server, which is precisely the work this feature exists to preserve. verdict.reason: Verified independently. `logout()` unconditionally runs `await eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` (packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:105), and `fetchWithAuth`'s 401 arm calls `logout({redirect:false, showSuccessToast:false, suppressFailure:true})` after a failed refresh (packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:228-236) — an involuntary session expiry, not a user action. None of those options reach the erase: `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` takes no arguments (offline-erase.ts:65) and its only early return requires `signedInUserId` to be unset, which cannot be the case for a signed-in user because `rememberOfflineUser(userId)` is set unconditionally by OfflineRuntime (offline-runtime.tsx:42) mounted by PrivateRoute (PrivateRoute.tsx:35). The erase is total: `dropAllForUser` purges every header entry AND `dropArchivesWhere(BY_USER, ...)` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:842-853), destroying the archived, unreconciled edits that `offerRecoverableWork`/`listRecoverableWork` exist to hand back in a later session (offline-runtime.tsx:106-176, offline-copy.ts:119). No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, no guard distinguishes deliberate logout, and the design doc's erase rationale concerns the user switching the setting off (docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:149-151) while its only mention of the 401 arm is a warning to avoid routing through it (:253). The comment at offline-erase.ts:42-44 acknowledges the 401 caller only to justify module-state identity, not to sanction destroying unsent work. In-lane for blast-radius (behaviour change to an exported symbol with an unconsidered second consumer) and blocking at major: silent, unrecoverable loss of locally persisted unsent edits on a routine token-expiry path.

finding.evidence: `supportsClientKey()` requires `@yorkie-js/react` >= 0.7.23 (packages/frontend/src/lib/yorkie-capabilities.ts, MinClientKeyVersion), and the pin is `"@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22"` (packages/frontend/package.json:65). `useDurableDocument` puts `supportsClientKey()` first in `eligible` (packages/frontend/src/lib/use-durable-document.ts), so no document is ever durable on this build. The new Settings section is not gated on the same capability: it renders unconditionally and its copy claims "Keeps edits that have not reached the server on this device, so they survive a reload or a crash while you are offline." A user who enables it gets no persistence at all, and the chip never reaches `saved-locally`. docs/tasks/active/20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:242-246 records the gate being closed as deliberate, but the user-visible switch is the one consumer not behind it.

verdict.reason: Every claimed fact checks out. supportsClientKey() compares the build-time pin against MinClientKeyVersion "0.7.23" (packages/frontend/src/lib/yorkie-capabilities.ts:24,61-67); vite.config.ts:360-364 injects that version verbatim from packages/frontend/package.json:65, which pins "@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22". atLeast("0.7.22","0.7.23") is false, so supportsClientKey() is permanently false on this build, and it is the first term of `eligible` in use-durable-document.ts:115-120 — meaning `durable` is never true, `clientKey` is never issued, and DurableYorkieProvider/WafflebaseDocStore never mount (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:38 says exactly this). The Settings Offline section at packages/frontend/src/app/settings/page.tsx:98-117 renders unconditionally with no capability gate and wires only setOfflinePersistenceEnabled, while its copy (lines 105-109) promises that unsent edits survive a reload or crash and that disabling deletes what was stored — two promises nothing on this build keeps. I found no guard, route condition, or caller that hides or disables this section; PrivateRoute.tsx:35 only mounts OfflineRuntime. This is in the blast-radius lane: the capability gate is honoured by every other consumer of the offline preference and bypassed by the one user-facing consumer, leaving a control that silently does nothing. The repository's own design doc (docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:394-403) independently names this state as the thing to avoid ("A control that ships before its behavior is not a dark launch; it is a control that does nothing"). Major: user-visible false durability promise on a reachable path.

verdict.reason: The conditional wrapping is present exactly as claimed: collab-document-provider.tsx:203-226 returns `inner` bare when not durable and `<DurableYorkieProvider>{inner}</DurableYorkieProvider>` when durable, so a `durable` flip changes the element type at that position and remounts the entire DocumentProvider subtree plus the Yorkie client (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:41-47). The flip is reachable mid-session: `eligible` depends on `useOfflinePersistenceEnabled()` (use-durable-document.ts:109-120), a live useSyncExternalStore subscribed to both a same-tab event and the cross-tab `storage` event (offline-persistence-preference.ts:102-121); the Settings switch toggles it with no reload gate (app/settings/page.tsx:111-115), and `standDown` via `onLockRefused` flips it in-tab (use-durable-document.ts:184-194, collab-document-provider.tsx:222). The repo's own test asserts "becomes durable without a reload" (use-durable-document.test.tsx:156-170). The unshown consumers explicitly rely on the opposite invariant — docs-view.tsx:577-582 and notes-view.tsx:174-179 both document that the Yorkie document "belongs to the enclosing DocumentProvider and outlives this effect". No guard prevents the toggle while an editor is open. This is an invariant other modules assume, violated where they read it — in lane, and major (editor teardown with queued-but-unsynced edits in the discarded client).

It is now called from `watchForOfflineDisable` (packages/frontend/src/lib/offline-erase.ts) the moment the Settings switch goes off — a cross-tab event, so a tab with a durable document attached can have its live entry deleted underneath it, and from `appendChange`'s point of view the missing header is the contract's silent "no base" success (the key is never added to `evicted`, so no rejection is raised to make the SDK re-base).

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. `collectStale` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:876) and `evictOldest` (:1045) both skip keys for which `isLive` (:306-311) is true, precisely to avoid purging under a live SDK client. `dropAllForUser` (:842-846) loops over every header key for the user and calls `purge` (:733-741) with no liveness check and without adding the key to `this.evicted` (contrast :1055), so a later `appendChange` hits the missing-header branch (:540-541, :560-563) and `refuseIfEvicted` (:617-620) returns silently — the SDK is told the write succeeded. The path is reachable with editors attached: `watchForOfflineDisable` calls `eraseOfflineData` → `dropAllForUser` (offline-erase.ts:161, :30), and its subscription includes a cross-tab `storage` listener (offline-persistence-preference.ts:104) while `OfflineRuntime`, which installs the watcher (offline-runtime.tsx:56), is mounted in every authenticated tab, including one holding a durable client (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:86-97). The same store even receives `isOpenElsewhere: isOpenInAnyTab` (offline-runtime.tsx:50), which `dropAllForUser` never consults. This is a guard with a reachable bypass at a different entry point — squarely the blast-radius lane — and the existing tests (wafflebase-doc-store-cleanup.test.ts:98, :111) cover only idle entries, so nothing refutes it.

finding.summary: Workspace deletion and member removal bypass the new offline purge, leaving local document copies after access is gone
finding.evidence:
The change adds `purgeOfflineDocuments` to `deleteDocument` (packages/frontend/src/api/documents.ts:167) and `deleteDocuments` (:215) on the stated rule that "content must not outlive the authority to read it" — which `docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:215` states as "Document deleted, **or workspace access lost** | Drop that entry". Two other frontend entry points reach exactly that outcome and do not purge:

- `deleteWorkspace(id)` — packages/frontend/src/api/workspaces.ts:88. `Document.workspace` is `onDelete: Cascade` (packages/backend/prisma/schema.prisma:125-126), so deleting a workspace deletes every document in it server-side while every locally persisted snapshot/changelog for those documents stays in IndexedDB until the 30-day sweep.
- `removeMember(...)` — packages/frontend/src/api/workspaces.ts:98. The removed member loses read authority for every document in that workspace; their on-disk copies remain.

A repo-wide grep shows `purgeOfflineDocuments` has exactly two call sites, both in `api/documents.ts`.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `purgeOfflineDocuments` has exactly two production call sites (packages/frontend/src/api/documents.ts:167, :215); the underlying primitives are equally unreachable from any workspace path — `WafflebaseDocStore.purgeDocument` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:759) is called only from offline-erase.ts:102, and `dropAllForUser` only from eraseOfflineData (offline-erase.ts:30), reached from logout and the preference-off watcher. `deleteWorkspace` (api/workspaces.ts:88) and `removeMember` (api/workspaces.ts:98) import nothing from @/lib/offline-erase, and their mutations (app/workspaces/workspace-settings.tsx:132-141, :181-197) only invalidate queries, navigate and toast. No access-loss purge exists anywhere else: no 403/404 purge in durable-yorkie-provider.tsx, and the only workspace-aware text in lib/ is a comment (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:726) describing the very trigger that has no caller. The invariant is a genuine project contract (docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:215 lists "Document deleted, or workspace access lost | Drop that entry"), and the change's own rationale (api/documents.ts:165) rejects the 30-day sweep as sufficient collection, so the sweep is not a guard here. This is a reachable bypass of a newly established invariant at a site outside the diff — in lane, major. Caveat: the `removeMember` half is not fixable client-side, since the purge runs in the removing user's browser and cannot reach the removed member's device; only the `deleteWorkspace` half is actionable.

finding.summary: logout()'s new erase is a no-op on any route where PrivateRoute never mounted, so signing out can leave document content on a shared device
finding.evidence: `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` (packages/frontend/src/lib/offline-erase.ts:65) erases nothing unless module state `signedInUserId` was set, and the only writer is `rememberOfflineUser(userId)` in `OfflineRuntime` (packages/frontend/src/components/offline-runtime.tsx:42), mounted solely by `PrivateRoute`. `logout()` is also reached from `fetchWithAuth`'s 401 arm at packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:229, which runs on every authenticated request from routes registered *outside* `PrivateRoute` — `/shared/:token`, `/t/:id`, `/templates`, `/harness/*` (packages/frontend/src/App.tsx:107-127). A user who enabled offline persistence and wrote entries in an earlier session, then opens a share link directly in a fresh tab and has the session expire there, is signed out with `signedInUserId === undefined` and every stored snapshot left on disk — the exact case the per-device setting exists to protect. The fix belongs on the new code (record the identity from a place that covers every authenticated route, or derive it in `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout`).

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` early-returns unless module state `signedInUserId` is set (offline-erase.ts:65-70); the sole production writer is `rememberOfflineUser` called from `OfflineRuntime` (offline-runtime.tsx:42, cleared at :89), which is mounted only by `PrivateRoute` (PrivateRoute.tsx:35). `logout()` (auth.ts:81, erase at :105) is also invoked from `fetchWithAuth`'s 401 arm (auth.ts:229), which is reachable from routes registered outside `PrivateRoute`: `/t/:id`, `/templates`, `/shared/:token` (App.tsx:119-126). Concretely, `template-landing.tsx:110` calls `createFromTemplate`, which uses `fetchWithAuth` (api/templates.ts:1,187), and the file's own comment at template-landing.tsx:114-116 confirms that path yields the AuthExpiredError/logout branch. In such a tab `signedInUserId` is undefined, so sign-out silently erases nothing while earlier-session snapshots remain in IndexedDB on the shared device. No alternative identity source or compensating erase trigger exists (grep over eraseOfflineData*/rememberOfflineUser found none). Bypass of a newly added cleanup guard on a reachable path from call sites outside the diff — in lane, major.
